name: deployment
prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Create a polished technical diagram on pure white, wide landscape about 1800 by 1200. Thin rounded outlines, restrained pastel blue purple orange green, very legible dark sans-serif labels and generous spacing. Title exactly: Three interfaces for robot deployment. Three clearly separated horizontal rows, with NO arrows between rows. Row 1 blue heading RMA: adapt to physics. Left to right: State + action history -> Context estimate -> Fast policy -> a small clear quadruped robot on uneven ground. Add a separate Current state input arrow into Fast policy. Row 2 purple heading UMI: align demonstrations. Left to right: a human hand holding a camera-equipped gripper -> Relative poses + timestamps -> Robot policy -> a small robot arm with gripper. Row 3 orange heading RTC: execute while generating. Two aligned horizontal bands: upper band Current actions executing, lower band Next chunk generating, overlapping in time; both lead at right to a box Aligned handover. Keep timing bands qualitative without numerical ticks. Footer: Physics context / Observation-action interface / Chunk continuity. These are complementary system views, not one serial algorithm. Do not draw a shared controller, common training loss, or connections between different rows. Only use the quoted short labels. All arrows must terminate on their intended boxes, not on text. No photographs, no heavy shadows, no logos, no watermark.
review: Superseded in the article by deployment-inputs-v2, which makes previous-action and image inputs explicit. This initial asset is preserved.

name: residual
prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. A precise clean robotics control block diagram on pure white background, landscape 1800 by 1100. Thin rounded outlines, muted pastel blue purple orange green, generous spacing, large dark sans-serif English labels. Title: Residual reinforcement learning. Main runtime feedback loop: a left box State branches to upper blue Fixed controller and lower purple Residual policy. BOTH outputs enter one central circle labelled +. From this sum go to orange Execution limits, then green Robot + contact environment on the right. There is exactly one + combining the two branches. A bottom return arrow from Robot + contact environment goes back to State, labelled Feedback. In a separated bottom panel heading Training, show Recorded transitions -> Replay buffer -> TD3 updates, with an update arrow going ONLY to Residual policy, never to Fixed controller. A small Reward input enters TD3 updates. Distinguish solid Runtime arrows and dashed Training arrows with a clear legend. The fixed controller is fixed for this diagram. Do not claim stability, safety, automatic force limits, or independent optimization of two reward terms. The execution limits box is an interface, not a formal safety guarantee. Keep all labels short, no equations, no decorative plot, no crossing text or lines.
review: Accepted after label/arrow, source, desktop/mobile, zoom and native-PDF review: runtime sum feeds execution interface; TD3 update targets residual policy only. No stability guarantee is inferred.

name: contact
prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Create a clean, accurate technical overview of active robot-environment calibration, pure white background, wide landscape 1800 by 1100. Thin rounded outlines, subdued pastel blue purple orange green, dark legible sans-serif labels, generous whitespace. Title: Calibrate by touching and sliding. Main workflow left to right across two spacious rows if needed: Pose hypotheses -> Choose surface normal -> Compliant touch + slide -> Contact / no contact -> SDF likelihood -> Resample poses. Draw a clear return arrow from Resample poses to Pose hypotheses. Add a separate Known environment geometry box with an arrow to SDF likelihood. Add Joint encoders + force/torque as a small input box into Contact / no contact. Show a small robot arm gently touching a rigid stepped surface next to the Compliant touch + slide box, with a tangent arrow along the surface labelled Slide and a perpendicular arrow labelled Normal. Show several translucent frame hypotheses near the first box and a tighter cluster at resampling, without numerical error claims. At bottom a separate checking panel: Spread / Stability / Contact consistency -> Continue or stop. No cameras, no tactile skin, no learned policy block, no entropy maximization block, no exact point-contact localization. All arrows clearly connect the correct modules. Only use these short English labels. No photograph, no logos, no watermark.
review: Accepted after label/arrow, source, desktop/mobile, zoom and native-PDF review: known geometry feeds SDF compatibility weights; contact event and encoded robot state do not claim a separately measured precise contact point. Normal diversity is a heuristic, not explicit entropy optimization.

name: deployment-inputs-v2

name: rma-training-stages
prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Create a precise clean RMA training/deployment diagram, white background, large landscape canvas around 2000 by 1500. Thin rounded outlines, restrained pastel blue purple orange green, dark very legible sans-serif English labels, generous spacing. Three spacious horizontal panels with NO gradient/update arrows across panels. Main title: RMA: learn a context, then infer it. Panel 1 title: Phase 1: privileged training. Show Environment factors -> Trainable encoder -> z -> Trainable base policy -> Joint targets. A separate Current state + previous action box also enters Trainable base policy. A clear bottom label PPO updates encoder and base policy, with dashed update arrows to BOTH trainable boxes. Panel 2 title: Phase 2: adaptation training. Its main horizontal row shows State-action history -> Trainable adapter -> z_hat -> Frozen base policy -> Simulated rollouts. A return arrow from Simulated rollouts goes to State-action history, labelled Collect current-policy history. A separate row above the main row shows Environment factors -> Frozen encoder -> Target z. Target z and z_hat BOTH enter a small MSE loss box. From MSE loss exactly one dashed update arrow goes to Trainable adapter ONLY. Draw NO update arrow to Frozen encoder or Frozen base policy. Add a small Current state + previous action input arrow into Frozen base policy if space permits; keep all connections clear and noncrossing. Panel 3 title: Deployment: fixed network weights. Show State-action history -> Adapter 10 Hz -> Latest z_hat -> Base policy 100 Hz -> PD + robot. A separate Current state + previous action input arrow enters Base policy 100 Hz. Feedback from PD + robot returns to State-action history. No environment factor input and NO training/update arrows in deployment. Use purple outlines/fills for trainable modules, pale blue for frozen modules, green for robot/rollouts; label the modules so color is not the only cue. Small legend: Solid arrows: data or control. Dashed arrows: weight updates. Do not add a camera, terrain map, physical-parameter labels for z, online fine-tuning, safety claims, numerical success rates or shared losses. Every arrow must terminate clearly at the intended box. Labels short, correctly spelled, no logos or watermark.
edit_prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit, scientific diagram correction. Edit target: the supplied RMA training/deployment diagram. Correct ONLY the solid data arrows in the middle Phase 2 panel; preserve every word, every box, all colors, the full top/bottom panels, legend and canvas. The predicted latent z_hat green box at the center of Phase 2 MUST feed BOTH the MSE loss and the Frozen base policy. Keep its existing upward branch into MSE loss. Add a clear direct horizontal solid black arrow from the RIGHT edge of that green z_hat box to the LEFT edge of the blue Frozen base policy box, at the boxes' vertical midpoint, with arrowhead on Frozen base policy. The line can pass below the MSE box but must not go through any box or text. REMOVE the current incorrect solid branch that rises from the bottom Collect current-policy history feedback line into Frozen base policy. That bottom feedback line must connect only Simulated rollouts back to State-action history. Keep the dashed MSE update arrow pointing ONLY to Trainable adapter, and keep Current state + previous action pointing down into Frozen base policy. Do not change the other panels, labels or layout. Required middle-panel connections: history -> adapter -> z_hat -> frozen policy -> simulated rollouts -> history; target z and z_hat -> MSE; MSE dashed arrow -> adapter only. No feedback-line input into frozen policy.
candidate_review: Rejected: phase-2 policy input branched incorrectly from the rollout-history return rather than the predicted latent.
review: Accepted after checking every arrow: phase1 PPO updates encoder and policy; phase2 predicted latent feeds loss and frozen policy, simulated rollouts return to history, MSE updates adapter only; deployment uses fixed weights with adapter10Hz and policy100Hz.
